headline: 艾未未雪梨港辦新作
context: 中國藝術家艾未未（Ai Weiwei）在雪梨港推出新作《Mushrooms》，是一座40公尺高的雕塑。他在採訪中談到戰爭、和平與世界局勢，並表示「九成的藝術都是垃圾，真正的藝術要挑戰既有秩序」。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: From his farm in Portugal, the acclaimed artist speaks about war, peace, the state of the world – and his 40 metre sculpture Mushrooms, on Sydney Harbour “It’s like a film set. Like it’s not real,” the bemused Uber driver says as we pass through a succession of silent rural villages washed with milky sunlight. He’s right: signs of human life are weirdly absent during our windy journey through the Alentejo. I’m making my way to Ai Weiwei’s secluded farm, nestled deep in the Portuguese countryside, where arguably the world’s best known living artist has quietly lived for the last six years. When I arrive, I am ushered inside a vast cathedral of a building, a replica of Ai’s erstwhile, and controversially demolished , studio in Shanghai. The space is cavernous. It’s gridded by huge wooden columns and its dizzyingly high ceilings are webbed with beams. There is no artwork on the walls, nor are there any obvious signs of production or activity. voice_text: 艾未未在雪梨港，推出了一座40公尺高的新雕塑，叫《Mushrooms》。這位中國藝術家目前定居葡萄牙鄉間，他在採訪中談到戰爭、和平，還有他對世界局勢的看法。他說，九成的藝術都是垃圾，真正的藝術要挑戰既有秩序。
